Give Tippy tooltips a themed glass bubble without arrow

Spicetify.TippyProps renders bare .main-contextMenu-tippy with no client
styling, so page and playbar tooltips showed as unstyled text. Route our
tooltips through tippy's default render with an amai-lyrics theme, add the
missing bubble CSS (Spotify never loads tippy.css), and cover remaining
TippyProps tooltips with a fallback rule.

Fix FastDOM batching: reject-safe async helper, direct rAF scroll loop, awaited teardown

- Add src/utils/fastdomAsync.ts with measureAsync/mutateAsync (reject on

  installed explicitly in app.tsx main()

  direct scrollTop writes in the rAF loop keyed off rAF timestamps,
  skip zero-distance animations
- ScrollToActiveLine: drop layout-free outer fastdom batch, run guards
  synchronously into scrollIntoCenterView
- PageView: sync PageRoot lookup, awaited destroy before flag flip with
  full cleanup on missing node, createContextualFragment for PageHTML
- pageContent/pageControls/pageButtons: replace hand-rolled promise
  wrappers with mutateAsync/bare mutate, sync click feedback
- NowPlayingBarBackground: pendingUrl dedup, isConnected guards across
  the handoff, swaps batched via fastdom.mutate
- Add fastdomAsync and scrollIntoView tests

entry.title: fix(settings): restyle Amai preferences sections for Spotify 1.3
entry.content:
fix(settings): restyle Amai preferences sections for Spotify 1.3

Spotify 1.3.x hashed or removed the Encore class names that the vendored
spcr-settings markup copies (x-settings-*, x-toggle-*, main-dropDown-dropDown,
TypeElement-viola-textSubdued-type). Spicetify's css-map only maps theme CSS,
so the extension's sections lost every inherited style: rows collapsed to
display:block (controls fell below their labels), toggles degraded to bare UA
checkboxes with empty indicator spans, and the dropdown/input fell back to raw
browser widgets.

Move all preferences-page styling into src/css/Settings.css, scoped with
:is(#amai-settings, #amai-dev-settings, #amai-info) so it cannot leak into
Spotify's own rows, and restate the native look with metrics taken from the
shipped xpui-routes-desktop-settings.css: 2fr/1fr rows with a 24px gutter,
subdued 14px labels, the 42x24 switch (20px knob, #1db954 when on), the 32px
elevated dropdown that keeps the native caret, the Encore text input and the
small secondary button.

tests/settingsStyles.test.ts guards the seam: it extracts every hook class the
renderer emits and asserts the stylesheet styles it, so a class without a rule
cannot slip through again.

entry.title: refactor(lyrics): fold playbar gradient into the ArtworkSurfaces seam
entry.content:
refactor(lyrics): fold playbar gradient into the ArtworkSurfaces seam

The playbar's animated gradient ran a private artwork pipeline outside the
ArtworkSurfaces seam: its own 500ms skip-debounce (mirroring the seam's
FAN_OUT_DELAY_MS), its own spotify:image: rewrite (copy #2 of 3, ignoring
the shared normalizeImageUrl), and applyArtworkColors — structurally
identical to ArtworkColors.applyArtworkAccents (same 140 luminance floor,
same pad-to-5, same cached extractor). PlaybarLyrics.css already declared
--color-1..5: var(--amai-accent-1..5), so the private writes shadowed a
palette the seam already publishes with identical numbers.

Deleting it is strictly subtractive: the cover-art path (fetch + decode +
debounce) leaves the most-changed file in the repo, which had no tests.
Adds a regression test asserting the overlay never writes --color-* inline
and never fetches artwork, plus the jsdom requestAnimationFrame gap in the
shared test stub.

entry.title: Fix launch-waiter race in ArtworkSurfaces fan-out
entry.content:
Fix launch-waiter race in ArtworkSurfaces fan-out

The debounced fan-out snapshotted the cover URL at schedule time and
cleared the first-paint waiter unconditionally on fire. A song change
during the launch gap could then either overwrite the waiter's paint
with a stale blank or cancel the waiter while still blank, leaving the
theme empty until the next song change.

Re-read live at fire time and only clear the waiter when there is an
artwork URL to paint. Adds two regression tests covering both
interleavings.

entry.title: Deepen playback-time and artwork surfaces; paint theme on launch
entry.content:
Deepen playback-time and artwork surfaces; paint theme on launch

Playback-time (GetProgress.ts): shrink the interface to its deep seam.
Unexport reanchorPosition and destroyGetProgressLoop (zero external
callers), delete _DEPRECATED___GetProgress and SpotifyPlayer._DEPRECATED_.
Teardown now flows through lifecycle; mock factories and the
playbackPosition seam test cross the same small interface. The bespoke
variable-rate loop stays off IntervalManager (documented on the seam).

Artwork (new ArtworkSurfaces module): collapse the four-way debounced
fan-out behind mount/applyArtwork/refreshStaticSurfaces/cancelPending/
destroy with injectable adapters. SongChangeManager drops four debounced
fields for one call; app.tsx drops ~110 lines of observers for mount().
Fix launch gap where the theme stayed blank until the first song change:
mount parks a one-shot waiter for the first artwork URL.

Add CONTEXT.md PlaybackTime/ArtworkSurfaces terms.

  plain about-artist descendant)
- Scope random CSS vars to canvas element; cache-first lookups, no
  Array.from/contains in hot paths; single storage read; drop placeholder
  layers on load; single artwork metadata read per songchange
